newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page- April 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page- April 24.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Thursday:
* Encouraged by Bob Dole, more Republican senators said they were trying to find grounds to back the Chemical Weapons Convention when it goes to a vote on Thursday.

* Indonesia's Riady family, supporters of Bill Clinton, were attempting to acquire a multi-billion bank in California but backed away from the plan when they became involved in investigations into foreign donations made to the Democrats, according to their business associates in Hong Kong.
* Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori and former hostages provided more details of the meticulous plan to rescue 71 captives held by Marxist guerrillas in the Japanese Ambassador's residence in Lima.

* Former hostages freed in a dramatic rescue from a Japanese diplomatic residence in Lima indicated the raid's success was also due to the weakening of the captor rebel's unity and determination over the four-month seige.
* Two New Jersey teenagers suspected of fatally shooting two pizza delivery men Saturday night fantasized about murder and allegedly killed just for the sake of it, police said.

* A woman 63 years and nine months old recently gave birth to a healthy baby girl, by using a donated egg from a younger woman. The birth raises questions about whether there should be an age limit for pregnancy.
* The U.S. Energy Department announced that refrigerators sold in 2001 would have to use 30 percent less electricity than those on the market now.
